summary.name: HumanLayer
summary.one_liner: HumanLayer is a multiplayer coding agent IDE and cloud that brings agent sessions, plan artifacts, and code diffs together so teams can collaborate on AI-driven software work.
use_cases: Running multiple Claude Code or Codex sessions in parallel
Reviewing and commenting on AI-generated design docs with a team
Breaking a large coding task into research, design, and plan phases before implementation
Running long-running agent work on cloud daemons while the laptop is closed
Organizing agent sessions, worktrees and artifacts per task
summary.what_it_does: HumanLayer groups agent sessions, research, designs, plans and code diffs into tasks that a team can share and comment on. It offers a six-phase workflow (questions, research, design, structure, plan, implement) with checkpoints for human review. Design docs accept inline comments from both humans and agents, and those comments feed back into the agent work. A local daemon can run many agent sessions in parallel on a laptop, and cloud daemons can run longer jobs; the UI is described as available on web, desktop, or phone. Users bring their own Claude Code, Codex, or other AI subscriptions or API keys.
notable: Comment-driven design reviews where humans and agents comment inline on design docs
Six-phase RPI-style workflow with human checkpoints
Local and remote daemons syncing through a HumanLayer API
Bring-your-own-key model for Claude Code, Codex and others
caveats: Pro and Enterprise tiers are paid; the Starter plan is free for teams of three or less with up to 200 sessions per month
Not open source yet; only some building blocks, plus the RPI framework, are open source
Only some agents are listed (Claude Code, Codex, Copilot, Fireworks), and it supports some RPI and experimental workflows; bringing your own skills is described as in progress
